keyVerseText: In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened. windows: or, floodgates
rootMeaning: The Hebrew word חֹדֶשׁ (chôdesh) derives from the root חָדַשׁ (châdash), which means to be new, renew, or repair. This etymology highlights the concept of newness or renewal inherent in the term, going beyond the simple English gloss of 'month.' It suggests a cyclical restoration or a fresh beginning, emphasizing not only the measurement of time but also the spiritual and physical renewal associated with the new moon.
usageInScripture: Throughout Scripture, חֹדֶשׁ is predominantly used to denote a 'month' or the 'new moon,' appearing 283 times with the most frequent translations being 'month' (113 occurrences) and 'day of the month' (49 occurrences). This consistency reveals its primary function as a temporal marker tied to the lunar calendar, often carrying religious significance as the new moon was a time of worship and festival. The term also encompasses the first day of the lunar month, connecting the concept of newness with the start of a new cycle.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, חֹדֶשׁ embodies the divine rhythm of renewal established by God in creation, reflecting His sovereign ordering of time. This cyclical newness points believers to the continual opportunity for spiritual renewal and restoration in their walk with God. The new moon as a sacred time underscores God's provision for regular remembrance and worship, inviting His people to reflect on His faithfulness and mercy. Understanding חֹדֶשׁ enriches our appreciation of God's design for temporal order and the spiritual significance embedded in His appointed times.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 7:11 states, 'In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.' Here, חֹדֶשׁ situates the flood within God's divinely appointed time, emphasizing the precise moment in the lunar calendar when judgment began. The word's meaning as a new moon or month highlights the ordered progression of God's plan, reminding us that even catastrophic events unfold under His sovereign timing.
